name: Reissner-Nordstrom: the effective potential is repulsive (Phi > 0) only inside r < Q^2/2M, which lies inside the horizon at every Q

published_statement: Hamilton & Lisle, gr-qc/0411060v2 p.5, Sec II.B: 'In this case the mass M(r) = M - Q^2/(2r) interior to r ... can be interpreted as the mass M at infinity, less the mass INT_r^oo (E^2/8pi) 4 pi r^2 dr = Q^2/(2r) contained in the electric field E = Q/r^2 outside r. The RN geometry exhibits both outer and inner horizons r_+ and r_-, r_+- = M +- (M^2 - Q^2)^{1/2} (21). The inflow velocity beta hits the speed of light at the outer horizon r_+, reaches a maximum velocity between the outer and inner horizons, slows back down to the speed of light at the inner horizon r_-, and slows all the way to zero velocity at the turnaround radius r_0 = Q^2/2M (22). ... The RN solution describes the geometry of empty space surrounding a classical point charge of infinitesimal size, and as such consists of a gravitationally repulsive singularity of infinite negative mass sheathed in an electric field containing an infinite positive mass ... The infall velocity beta is imaginary inside the turnaround radius r_0 ..., the interior mass M(r) being negative inside this radius.' Faraoni & Vachon 2006.10827v2 p.5: PG coordinates fail 'in the inner region of the Reissner-Nordstrom metric ... [which has] a negative quasilocal mass ... since gravity becomes repulsive, a massive test particle with zero initial velocity cannot overcome this repulsion'; p.13: the breakdown occurs 'in any region with negative Misner-Sharp-Hernandez mass'. The Q <= M bound (Khuri-Weinstein 1307.5499 Thm 2, restating GHHP83): 'Let (M, g, k, E) be initial data for the Einstein-Maxwell equations with a strongly asymptotically flat end, and satisfying the charged dominant energy condition, then m >= |Q|', with the charged DEC 'mu_0 >= |J| + |rho|' (eq 2). McCormick 1907.07967 p.14: 'Clearly we can write down initial data with very small mass density and very large charge density, and then one should not expect this inequality to hold', and m >= |Q| needs the pointwise (3.16) R(g) - 2|E|^2 >= 4|div E|.
published_hypotheses: Reissner-Nordstrom electrovac: source-free Maxwell field on r > 0, static spherically symmetric, geometric Gaussian units (Hamilton-Lisle Sec II.B)
the stated ordering r_0 = Q^2/2M inside r_- <= r_+ presupposes real horizons, i.e. |Q| <= M (eq 21); the paper treats 'a spherical black hole of mass M and charge Q'
r = 0 is a singular centre ('a gravitationally repulsive singularity of infinite negative mass'); the region r < r_0 is where the Misner-Sharp interior mass is negative
'repulsive' = negative Misner-Sharp-Hernandez mass (Faraoni-Vachon pp.5, 13): an E = 1 radial geodesic cannot enter; this is exactly f > 1, i.e. Phi > 0

for the Q <= M bound charge.py adds: complete Einstein-Maxwell data with a strongly asymptotically flat end AND the charged dominant energy condition mu_0 >= |J| + |rho| (matter energy density dominates matter CHARGE density), per KW13 eq (2) / McCormick (3.16)

for any positivity route to a horizonless body: dominant energy condition, untrapped hypersurface, REGULAR centre (Hayward Prop 6); 'the energy can be negative if the above assumptions do not hold' (p.9)
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED -- 'up to extremal'. phase1.py:405-407 states 'Phi > 0 only inside r < Q^2/2M, which is hidden at every Q (charge.py)'. charge.py's own check is labelled 'hidden at every charge up to extremal' and samples only q in {0.1,0.5,0.9,0.99,1.0} (charge.py:193-195), and charge.py's predicate positive_region_is_hidden (charge.py:127-130) returns False for every Q > M because horizon() is None there (charge.py:122-125) -- rederive C3 calls the owner's own functions read-only: False at q = 1.01, 1.5, 2, 10. The source (Hamilton-Lisle eq 21-22) states the ordering only for a black hole, |Q| <= M.

DROPPED -- the charged dominant energy condition and completeness/asymptotic flatness behind 'Q <= M'. charge.py:28-32 (and 198-200, 274-276) extends 'hidden' to every Q by 'the POSITIVE ENERGY THEOREM FOR EINSTEIN-MAXWELL (Gibbons & Hull; Witten) forces Q <= M, so there is no charged configuration anywhere with a VACUUM region of positive potential'. KW13 Thm 2 / eq (2) and McCormick (3.16) (READ) force m >= |Q| only for complete AF data whose matter density dominates its charge density; every laboratory charged body violates that (rederive C9: 1 kg carrying 1 nC has Q/M = 11.6; the electron 2.04e21), and rederive C6 exhibits a static Einstein-Maxwell shell with positive rest mass and Q/M = 16.67. Same finding as the sibling audit gibbons-hull-1982-witten-1981-positive-energy-einstein-maxwell (NARROWED); 'Witten' as an author of the charged bound is an attribution discrepancy (Witten 1981 is the uncharged theorem), not a refutation.

DROPPED (unnamed) -- a regular-centre / no-naked-singularity hypothesis. charge.py:29-30 'no charged configuration anywhere with a VACUUM region of positive potential' is literally false for the superextremal RN electrovac solution itself: rederive C4 (z3) shows M = 1, Q = 2 has f > 0 for every r > 0 (no horizon) and Phi(1) = +1 in vacuum; it is excluded only by GHHP completeness or Hayward's regular-centre hypothesis (its Misner-Sharp mass -> -oo at r -> 0+, C4). The tree nowhere names this hypothesis at the phase1/charge sites.

REPLACED ROUTE (the conclusion survives, the cited reason does not cover it) -- for horizonless bodies charge.py:30-32 argues 'A horizonless charged body must have matter out past where the horizon would be, so the r < Q^2/2M region is inside its matter'. For Q > M there is no 'where the horizon would be'. What actually covers every Q is Misner-Sharp positivity: static spherical symmetry, regular centre and rho_total >= 0 give m(R) >= 0 and then Phi < 0 on the whole vacuum exterior, including Q > M (rederive C5: rho = m'/(4 pi r^2) from G^t_t by sympy; the implication by z3 with Q > M allowed; Hayward Prop 6 is the dynamical form, READ). So the correct named hypotheses are 'static (or untrapped) spherical symmetry + regular centre + rho >= 0 (DEC in Hayward)', not 'Q <= M'. drivensource's N2 route ('needs no positive energy theorem', per the sibling audit) is where the tree states this; phase1/charge.py do not cite it here.

ADDED (in canonical.json's label, not in the owner lines) -- 'repulsive'. The owner lines say 'Phi > 0' / 'positive potential'. In the force sense a static test particle released at rest is pushed outward iff r < Q^2/M (rederive C7), twice the Phi > 0 radius; for Q <= M this is still inside r_+ (z3: Q^2/2M < r_- <= Q^2/M <= M <= r_+), but for an over-extremal positive-energy body it can lie in vacuum (shell witness: a = 10 < Q^2/M = 16.67, Phi < 0 there). This does not touch the tree's claim, which uses the sign of Phi (phase1.py:276 transition quantity int(1 - e^{-Phi}) dl), and Faraoni-Vachon use 'repulsive' for negative MSH mass exactly as the label does -- a naming discrepancy recorded, not a refutation.

STRENGTHENED relative to the tree (no drift against it): for 0 < |Q| <= M the Phi > 0 region lies inside the INNER horizon r_-, not only the outer one: r_c/r_- = (1 + sqrt(1 - q^2))/2 in [1/2, 1) (sympy; z3 negation unsat). Hamilton-Lisle's ordering (beta reaches c at r_- before zero at r_0) says the same.

UNNAMED REGIME HYPOTHESIS -- classical fields. For an elementary charge the classical RN exterior would put r_c = Q^2/2M = r_e/2 = 1.409e-15 m (rederive C9), larger than the ~1e-18 m class size bounds the sibling audit classical-charge-radius-inside-body READ (not re-read here), with no horizon; either the interior carries negative energy (Bonnor-Cooperstock, per that sibling audit) or classical Einstein-Maxwell does not apply below the Compton wavelength (3.86e-13 m, recalled). The tree's 'at every Q' implicitly assumes the classical regime; the magnitude at stake is Phi ~ 9.5e-37 at 1e-18 m.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis does not bite on the core result: Phi > 0 <=> r < Q^2/2M and Q^2/2M < r_- <= r_+ for |Q| <= M are closed-form consequences of the RN metric with no measured input (rederive C1-C2), and no datum discovered since 1916 can move them. What the authors of the SUPPORTING bound lacked is not data either: the electron's charge-to-mass ratio (Thomson 1897) already put ordinary matter outside the charged-DEC hypothesis by ~1e21 decades before GHHP 1983 (rederive C9), and a 1 kg body carrying 1 nC is 'over-extremal' (Q/M = 11.6) -- so the tree's extension to 'every Q' through Q <= M rests on a hypothesis real matter fails, a scope finding. Evidence the conclusion nonetheless survives for classical bodies: Misner-Sharp positivity under rho >= 0 and a regular centre excludes a vacuum Phi > 0 region at every Q (C5; shell witness C6). Evidence it does not survive everywhere: the bare superextremal RN electrovac has a visible vacuum Phi > 0 region (C4), and a classical point electron would have r_c = 1.409e-15 m outside the measured size bounds -- excluded only by a regular-centre hypothesis or by leaving the classical regime. Later data (lepton size bounds) sharpen that last point; they do not change the tree's downstream use (phase1's charge state Lambda = 0), since the magnitude is Phi ~ 1e-36.
grade_evidence: The published result (Hamilton-Lisle eq 21-22, READ; RN classics NAMED-NOT-READ) -- Phi > 0 only inside r < Q^2/2M, which lies inside the horizon -- is re-derived exactly for 0 < |Q| <= M, and sharper than the tree states: inside the inner horizon r_- (z3, rederive C2). The tree's 'hidden at every Q' (phase1.py:405-407) holds on a smaller class than stated: (i) it drops charge.py's own 'up to extremal' qualifier (charge.py:193), and charge.py's predicate returns False for every Q > M (C3); (ii) the extension to Q > M rests on 'Gibbons-Hull/Witten force Q <= M' (charge.py:28-32), whose charged dominant energy condition (KW13 eq 2, McCormick 3.16, READ) is dropped and is violated by all ordinary charged matter (C9) and by an explicit static shell (C6); (iii) the bare superextremal RN solution has a visible vacuum Phi > 0 region (C4), excluded only by an unnamed regular-centre / no-naked-singularity hypothesis. NOT WRONG: under the correctly named hypotheses -- static spherical symmetry, regular centre, rho_total >= 0 -- there is no vacuum Phi > 0 region at ANY Q (C5, Hayward Prop 6 READ), so the downstream use (phase1 CANDIDATES charge state Lambda = 0, excluded from ranked()) stands on that class; the literal counterexample (C4) lies outside it and a misattribution (Witten) is a discrepancy. NOT DATA-DEPENDENT: no datum enters (C1, C9). NOT OPEN: the restatements were read in full text and every finite claim is machine-checked.
